done.why: A thief took the three treasures I'd carried out of the coal mine. I got one painting home to the trophy case, then went into the maze after him and got lost. Dead ends kept looping back on me, and I didn't have the patience to map it.

about: There's a white house with a trophy case, and under it a cave country full of valuable things: a crystal trident, a jade figurine, a sapphire bracelet, a painting. Finding treasure is the easy part. Getting it home is the hard part, because there's a thief who robs you in the dark, a bat that carries you off, a chimney too narrow to take much up, and a coal mine where every room looks the same.

moments.note: 'keep going around the house' wasn't understood. I had to learn to type compass directions.
I killed the troll in two blows and he vanished in black fog. Very dramatic.
I looked in the mirror and an ugly person stared back. It made me laugh.
Touching the mirror made the earth rumble. The room looked the same, but I'd been moved somewhere else.
Twisting Passage north just printed 'Mirror Room' with no description. I couldn't tell if it was the same room or another one.
Poseidon's crystal trident on the shore, my first treasure.
The bat grabbed me and dropped me back in the Squeaky Room. Garlic from the lunch sack kept him off afterward.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' It told me exactly what to put down.
I thought I'd gone back to the Gas Room, but I dropped the sword and pump in the coal mine instead. Easy to lose track of where you are.
Going east in the coal mine brought me back to the same room. The mine rooms all look identical.
A seedy man walked through and took the trident, the jade and the bracelet all at once. I'd carried them a long way, and that was the opposite of keeping them safe.
The chimney's 'room for you, your lamp and one thing more' message named everything I was carrying. Very clear.
I put the painting in the trophy case. Finally one treasure was safe.
The garlic I'd left in the Studio turned up in the maze. Someone had moved it.
Going back east in the maze led to a dead end, not to where I came from. I couldn't retrace my steps.

wished: Ask the game in plain words where things were, like 'where is the garlic?' or 'which passages are open?'
Say 'keep going around the house' or 'go back' and have it understood
Chase the thief or find out where he took my treasures
See full room descriptions every time I come back, so I could tell identical-looking rooms apart
Mark my path through the coal mine and maze without spending my own belongings as breadcrumbs

lines.line: There is an ugly person staring back at you.
lines.why: A small joke at my expense. It made the place feel like it had personality.

lines.line: The bat grabs you by the scruff of your neck and lifts you away....
lines.why: A shock. Then it made me open the lunch sack and find the garlic.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: It told me what to drop instead of just saying no.

lines.line: A seedy-looking individual with a large bag just wandered through the room. On the way through, he quietly abstracted some valuables from your possession, mumbling something about "Doing unto others before..."
lines.why: The moment my goal of keeping the treasure safe fell apart. It was funny and infuriating at once.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear rule, stated kindly, and it gave me a way to get the painting home.

fun.why: The first half was great fun: troll fight, mirror teleport, the trident, beating the bat with garlic. Losing all three mine treasures to the thief, then getting lost in the maze, drained the fun.

engagement.why: I kept wanting to see what was next and to get my treasures home. Getting the painting into the case was satisfying. My interest only dropped once I was lost in the maze.

difficulty.why: Directions only, rooms that don't lead back the way you come, identical mine and maze rooms, and a thief who takes everything. Hard for someone who doesn't know the rules. The helpful refusals (heavy load, chimney) were the fair parts.

interestingness.why: The coal mine, the mirror that moves you, the bat dropping you in a fixed room, the chimney limit, and a thief who seemed to move my garlic. It felt like a living place with its own rules.

prose.why: Witty and vivid in places: the vandals 'with exceptional taste', the ugly person in the mirror, the thief's mumbling. Revisited rooms show only their name, which made me unsure where I was.
